peerMapping.justification: Three-run Kimi K3 consensus selected only the displayed peers: CL 74.0% with 3/3 replicate support; NATGAS 15.0% with 3/3 replicate support; COPPER 11.0% with 3/3 replicate support. Individual rationales state each economic relationship.

peers.name: WTI crude oil
peers.reason: WTI is the direct substitute and same underlying crude oil exposure as Brent, so it should dominate the peer basket. It captures the common crude drivers: global oil demand, inventories, OPEC supply decisions, geopolitical disruption, refining economics, and the dollar-sensitive commodity cycle, while leaving mainly the Brent-WTI benchmark spread as idiosyncratic difference.

peers.name: Natural gas
peers.reason: Natural gas is the nearest intra-energy peer: it shares heating and power-generation demand, weather sensitivity, geopolitical supply risk, and fuel-substitution economics with crude oil, though its supply dynamics differ enough to warrant a clearly smaller weight. Its 24-hour perp liquidity of 4.553 USD millions is adequate but far thinner than CL, reinforcing a moderate allocation.

peers.name: Copper
peers.reason: Copper is the cyclical industrial commodity that best captures the global manufacturing and growth cycle embedded in oil demand, and energy is a major input cost in copper mining and refining, linking the two through shared cost and macro channels. Its 24-hour perp liquidity of 7.656 USD millions supports execution at this modest weight.

primary_index_hedge.name: WTI crude oil
primary_index_hedge.reason: Although the legacy field is named primary_index_hedge, the best hedge here is a commodity, not an index. WTI crude oil is the closest hedge for Brent because both are crude oil benchmarks with the same underlying energy exposure; the residual difference is mainly grade, location, transport, and regional supply. CL also has higher displayed 24-hour perp liquidity than BRENTOIL, 102.282 USD millions versus 73.627 USD millions, which is an execution advantage only and not the source of the economic similarity.

peerMapping.historyMethod: daily-rebalanced peer spot total returns using the fixed Kimi weights; the basket begins with the first available selected peer, unavailable pre-listing peers are omitted, and remaining weights are renormalized; the browser rebases the basket to the target spot level at the first shared date of each selected chart range

liveSplice.method: current Hyperliquid native or TradeXYZ perp mid divided by that peer's matching-venue perp close on its latest spot date; available Kimi weights are renormalized and applied as a one-period return from the published peer spot endpoint; USD cash close is retained for disclosure but never mixed with a differently scaled perp contract

underlierSelection.method: highest summed live contract volume; open interest and contract count break ties

model.name: ATM-straddle-implied lognormal distribution
model.description: Each target uses the nearest paired liquid ATM call and put. Their combined ask implies the expiration distribution shown on the chart.
model.measure: option-implied, not a historical or physical forecast
